$comment: Wikidata's own hierarchy properties, kept as themselves (#74 §C: 'Preserve
The three that mattered in MVP-0's `concept_relations.type` enum, plus the bridge
from an everyday concept to its taxon item. Q146 *cat* is a concept with an enwiki
article and no P171 at all; Q20980826 *Felis catus* is the taxon and carries the whole
chain to Animalia. P13176 is the one hop between them, and it is what made the taxon
chain reachable from a word in the first place.
Only P171 and P13176 are walked to closure by the importer. P279 and P31 are recorded
as edges and never chased: following them climbs out of biology into the abstract
ontology (40 seeds pulled 1,372 entities over 20 tiers before this was narrowed).
That policy lives in the adapter; these rows only say the edges are legal.
`entity/*` expands over every entity kind at seed time. An imported Wikidata item's
kind is not known before its statements are read, and enumerating 100 pairs by hand
per predicate would be a worse record of the same rule.
`cycles_allowed` is false for all four: a taxonomy that loops is a data defect, and
the recursive chain walk depends on it terminating.
`instance_of` also carries `sense/- -> sense/-` (#181): WordNet's instance_hypernym is
the same relation as P31, stated between meanings rather than things. It lives here
rather than in core.json because a predicate is declared once, and this is where it was.

predicates.description: Wikidata P171. The taxonomy proper, terminating at Animalia. The chain walk prefers this above all others.
Wikidata P279. The chain walk falls back to this where there is no parent taxon.

Wikidata P31, and WordNet's instance_hypernym (#181): a named individual filed under a class, always written instance -> class, so no inverse row exists and one predicate answers 'what are the instances of X' for both sources. Between entities it is followed only at the first step of a chain: following it at every step walks a named individual up to 'abstract entity'. Between senses it is WordNet's claim about a meaning, and the word page reads it from the object side (#181).
Wikidata P13176. The bridge from an everyday concept to the taxon item that carries its classification.
